# curlPro

> A Python HTTP client whose traffic carries a real browser's network fingerprint — TLS ClientHello, HTTP/2 and HTTP/3 frames, header set, order and case, WebSocket handshake — driven by JSON profiles, not code. Python `ctypes` over a Go library (uTLS, patched fhttp, vendored uquic) shipped inside the wheel. Apache 2.0. PyPI: `curlpro`. Repository: https://github.com/int3re/curlpro

This file is the entry point for an AI assistant. Read `docs/GUIDE.md` in full
before proposing code that touches this library; it is the verified reference
and it lists, in section 15, what the library already does so you do not
reimplement it. The README is the front page for people.

## The four rules

- Profiles are data: a browser is a `.json` file, the code is generic. A new browser version is a profile delta or `curlpro.register_profile()`, never a library change.
- Measured, not assumed: every profile value was seen on the wire from a real browser; where nothing was measured the library says so.
- Refuse rather than ignore: an option that cannot be honoured raises with the reason. Nothing is silently downgraded, dropped or substituted.
- The wire is the truth: `session.fingerprint()` and `session.audit()` are computed from the bytes that would go out, offline.

## Surface (all in `import curlpro`)

- `Session(impersonate="chrome-151-windows", *, verify, cert, trust_env, max_response_size, timeout, connect_timeout, response_timeout, proxy, default_headers, header_order, allow_redirects, max_redirects, cookies, force_http1, post_quantum, resume, http3, alt_svc, resolve, ip_version, keep_alive, hooks, device, devices, max_idle_conns, idle_conn_timeout, retries, retry_statuses, retry_methods, retry_backoff, retry_max_backoff, respect_retry_after, mode, page, credentials, samesite, preflight)`
- `s.request(method, url, *, headers, params, auth, data, json_body, files, fields, body_file, header_order, default_headers, cookies, session_headers, protocol, timeout, connect_timeout, response_timeout, allow_redirects, max_redirects, retries, retry_statuses, retry_methods, retry_backoff, retry_max_backoff, respect_retry_after, proxy, mode, page, credentials, preflight, expect, rollback_cookies)` and `get/post/put/patch/delete/head/options`
- `s.stream(...)` → `StreamResponse` (`iter_content`, `iter_lines`, `read`, `close`); `s.websocket(url, headers, subprotocols, timeout, max_message_size)` → `WebSocket` (`send`, `recv`, `ping`, `close`, iteration)
- `s.headers_for(method, url, *, headers, header_order, mode, page, credentials, protocol, default_headers, session_headers)` → the headers this request would carry, without sending it; HTTP/1.1 names in the wire's case, and that form by itself for an `http://` URL
- `s.preflight_for(method, url, *, headers, mode, page, credentials, protocol, session_headers)` → the CORS preflight a request would be preceded by, or `None` when a browser would send none
- `s.headers` (mapping; `= None` removes a profile header; `.suppressed`), `s.cookies` (mapping plus `all/set/load/export/save/load_file/save_netscape/load_netscape/to_netscape/snapshot/restore/transaction/clear`), `s.page` (the page requests are made from; `= None` clears), `s.hooks`, `s.on_request/on_response/on_error`, `s.fingerprint(url)`, `s.audit(mode=None)` (judges the sets requests actually went out with; `mode="fetch"` asks ahead), `s.close()`
- `Response`: `status ok proto headers header(name) content text encoding json(**kw) url history preflight preflights cookies elapsed raise_for_status()`; `headers` is a `Headers` (`dict[str, list[str]]` looked up by any case, `.first(name)`); `Preflight(url, status, headers, cached)` is the CORS preflight that preceded the request
- `AsyncSession` — the same API as coroutines, native concurrency (goroutines, one thread)
- `Expect(status, not_status, body, not_body, headers, not_headers, non_empty, json, encoding)` → `ExpectationFailed`
- `Persona.new/load/save/session/open/capture/fingerprint/audit/to_dict/from_dict`, `load_all(dir)`
- `Fingerprint`: `ja4 ja4_r ja3n ja3 ja3_text akamai ciphers extensions curves sigalgs alpn headers headers_http1 ja4h ja4h_http1 ja4h_available user_agent profile device devices measured source client_hello to_dict() diff()`; `to_dict()` also carries `mode`, `modes_used`, `derived_fetch`
- `Finding(code, level, what, why, fix)`; `audit(session_or_persona)`
- `Profile.from_file(path).derive(name, **overrides).register()`; `load_profiles(dir)`, `register_profile(x)`, `list_profiles(measured=None)` (`True`: the 42 captured whole; `False`: the 260 with any part not measured), `ensure_loaded()`
- `capabilities(name)` → `{modes, protocols, devices, client_hints, websocket, http1_set, user_agent, user_agent_varies, derived_fetch, fetch_metadata, cookies, measured, source, name, based_on, family}` (`measured`: captured from a browser, here or by the imported signatures; `source`: for a transcribed profile, where from and what was taken) (`fetch_metadata`: whether `sec-fetch-*` is sent at all — Safari 15 has a fetch set and none; `cookies`: the family's policy `{lax_by_default, lax_post_seconds, none_requires_secure, third_party, schemeful}`, absent for a library); `get_profile(name)` → `Profile` (inheritance resolved, `.data`); `library_version()` → the native library's version
- Module-level `request/get/post/put/patch/delete/head/options(url, impersonate=..., **kw)`; every verb's `**kw` is typed (`Unpack[curlpro.RequestKwargs]`), so mypy and editors check the names; `DEFAULT_MAX_RESPONSE_SIZE` (100 MiB) caps a buffered response when `max_response_size` is not given, streams are not capped; a request whose reused keep-alive connection dies before any response byte is resent once on a new connection, any method (Chromium's rule); `rollback_cookies` undoes exactly the request's own cookie changes; exceptions are declared in the public `curlpro.errors`; `capabilities()["device_kind"]` and `fingerprint().device_kind` say what a pool holds (`phone`, `desktop`, `iphone`, `distro`)
- Exceptions: `CurlProError(.code)` ← `Timeout`, `HTTPError(.status, .response)`, `ExpectationFailed(.response)`, `WebSocketClosed`, `ProxyError(.stage, .status)`, `CORSError(.status, .headers, .reason, .method, .url)`, and `PermanentError` ← `ProfileCapabilityError`, `ConfigurationError`, `ProxyAuthError` (also a `ProxyError`). Codes: `timeout expectation profile_capability configuration proxy proxy_auth proxy_closed cors session_closed too_large ws_closed ws_too_big ws_protocol`
- Retry logic: `except curlpro.PermanentError` means never retry (the profile cannot, the arguments are wrong, or the proxy rejected the login); `Timeout`, a `ProxyError` at stage `dial`/`connect` and an uncoded `CurlProError` are worth a retry; a `CORSError` is decided by its `.status` (a 503 to the OPTIONS passes, a missing `Access-Control-Allow-Origin` does not).
- `curlpro.requests`: a `requests`-shaped face (`get`, `Session`, `status_code`); unsupported arguments raise

## Facts an assistant tends to get wrong

- Adding any custom header switches the request to the browser's fetch header set in `mode="auto"`; that is correct. `mode="navigate"` overrides.
- To drop one profile header use `headers={"Name": None}`, not `default_headers=False` (which also drops the User-Agent and the order).
- Never hand-write `Referer`, `Origin` or `sec-fetch-site`: set `s.page = url` (or `page=` on a request) and the three are derived as Chrome and Firefox derive them; a hand-written Referer beside `sec-fetch-site: none` is an audit finding.
- `AsyncSession` proxies everything `Session` has, `page`/`fingerprint`/`audit`/`headers_for`/`preflight_for` included, and its responses carry `history`, `preflights` and `elapsed` like the sync ones (they did not until 0.10.1), and refuses unknown attributes (`__slots__`) — a silently swallowed `s.page = url` is what made that necessary.
- Cookies from a page follow the browser: `credentials` defaults to `same-origin` (no cookies to another origin, even of the same site — the default of `fetch()` and XHR); `include` applies the `SameSite` rules of the family (Chromium: Lax by default with the two-minute POST window; Firefox and Safari: no third-party cookies on a fetch at all); `samesite=False` sends every match as before 0.10. Never filter the `Cookie` header by hand. A response to a request made without credentials (`omit`, or the default `same-origin` to another origin) sets no cookie, as in a browser; a preflight's `Set-Cookie` is ignored too.
- A non-simple cross-origin fetch from a page (a method beyond GET/HEAD/POST, `application/json`, any custom header) is preceded by the browser's CORS preflight automatically — checked, cached for `Access-Control-Max-Age`, refused as `CORSError` with the answer, and then the request is not sent. Never build the OPTIONS with `s.options(headers=...)`; `preflight=False` sends straight out.
- Along a redirect chain `Origin` is the chain's starting origin and turns `null` under the Fetch standard's redirect rule (Chromium also on a navigation POST after any cross-origin hop) — measured on both browsers, do not set it by hand.
- A transcribed profile is another project's claim, not a measurement: never treat it as evidence of what a browser version sends, and never let it into a random rotation without meaning to (`list_profiles(measured=True)`).
- Never probe to learn what a profile supports: `curlpro.capabilities(name)` answers it, and matching on error text is explicitly unsupported.
- TLS session resumption is on by default (measured on both browsers); `resume=False` turns it off. The first hello of a session never changes, so fingerprints are unaffected.
- `header_order=[..., "accept", "x-api-key", ...]` edits the browser's order in place; `...` is the profile's own order.
- `timeout` caps the whole request; `(connect, total)` is the pair; `response_timeout` is the wait for headers.
- `ja3` moves per connection on Chrome ≥110 (extension shuffling); compare `ja4` or `ja3n`.
- Bodies are already decompressed (gzip, deflate, br, zstd) and `r.text` already has the charset detected.
- 302 profiles: 42 captured whole, 14 captured but for their HTTP/2 SETTINGS (Chrome 98–116, Chrome 99 Android, Edge 98–101, Safari 15.3/15.5: their signatures recorded none, and until 0.12 an empty SETTINGS frame went out; the values are wreq-util's, marked `source.covers = ["http2.settings"]`), 8 derived for the versions current on 2026-09-26 (chrome-154-windows/macos/linux, edge-154-windows, opera-136-windows/macos, safari-27-ios/macos: `source.kind = "derived"`, a captured twin's hello under the new User-Agent and brands), all of them together 17 distinct JA4 values, and 238 transcribed from `0x676e67/wreq-util` — each transcribed one replays a captured twin's hello under its own User-Agent and brands, carries a `source` block, reports `measured: False` in `capabilities()` and `transcribed_profile` in `audit()`; `list_profiles(measured=True)` leaves them out, and a scraper rotating profiles at random should use it. The captured 56: (the pre-Kyber Chromium group, Chrome 119–131 and Edge 119/120, flips between two JA4 spellings as its padding extension comes and goes with the ECH GREASE payload size, like the browsers); HTTP/3 sections on chrome-151-windows, chrome-152-windows, chrome-152-android, yandex-26.8-android; fetch sets on every browser profile (Safari's 11 are **derived** from the Fetch standard, not captured — `capabilities()["derived_fetch"]` and the audit's `derived_fetch_set` say so; okhttp, a library, has none); 46 phones on the two Android profiles; a chosen device is written into the User-Agent on both (on chrome-152-android by the owner's decision — stock Chrome ≥110 sends the reduced `Android 10; K`), and without `device=` the captured string goes out. Identity pools since 0.11 on the 151–153 Chromium desktops (Windows release/build/wow64, macOS version/CPU/build, Linux build — with the `client_hints` section measured on Chrome 153, STAGE19), the iOS Safari profiles (the iOS version; Safari 26 freezes the OS token at `18_7` and writes the version only in `Version/`) and the Firefox Linux profiles (the `Ubuntu; ` token): `device="random"` draws one for the session, `fingerprint().device` names it, without `device=` the capture machine's values go out; seed `scripts/identities.json`, generator `scripts/gen-identities.py`; `edge-153-windows` and macOS Safari have no pool.
- From a repository checkout call `curlpro.load_profiles("profiles")`; from the wheel nothing.
- Public echo services lie: postman-echo.com is behind Cloudflare, which rewrites `Accept-Encoding`. Judge headers on `python/tests/rawserver.py`.
